t.6.50.1: But that tiger among Rākṣasas, of vast prowess, still reeling with the intoxication of sleep, went along the royal highway, which was graced with splendour.
t.6.50.2: Surrounded by thousands of rākṣasas, the one most difficult to conquer then went forth, showered with a rain of flowers from the houses.
t.6.50.3: He beheld the vast and delightful palace of the lord of the Rākṣasas, spread over with networks of gold and dazzling to the eye like the sun.
t.6.50.5: Having approached his brother's house and entered its inner chamber, he saw his elder brother seated in the aerial chariot Puṣpaka, deeply troubled.
t.6.50.4: Then, entering that dwelling of the lord of the rākṣasas as the sun enters a mass of clouds, he saw from afar his elder brother seated on his throne, as Śakra beholds Svayambhū seated upon his seat.
t.6.50.6: Then Daśagrīva, seeing Kumbhakarṇa arrived, rose quickly and, overjoyed, drew him close to his side.
t.6.50.7: Then mighty Kumbhakarṇa bowed at the feet of his brother, who was seated on a couch, and said, "What is to be done?" Rāvaṇa, delighted, sprang up and embraced him.
t.6.50.8: Embraced by his brother and duly welcomed, Kumbhakarṇa took his place upon a splendid, celestial, excellent seat.
t.6.50.9: Then the mighty Kumbhakarṇa, having taken his seat, his eyes reddened with anger, spoke these words to Rāvaṇa.
t.6.50.11: Rāvaṇa, with his eyes slightly rolling, spoke these words to his brother Kumbhakarṇa, who stood there enraged.
t.6.50.10: Why, O king, have you so earnestly had me awakened? Tell me, from what does your fear arise? Who is it that shall be a dead man today?
t.6.50.13: This mighty Rāma, son of Daśaratha, accompanied by Sugrīva, has crossed the ocean with his army and is cutting away our very root.
t.6.50.12: O mighty one, a very long time has passed today while you lay sleeping. Living at ease, you do not know the fear that Rāma has caused me.
t.6.50.14: Ah, behold the forests and groves of Laṅkā! Having come easily by way of the bridge, the monkeys have turned them into a single sea of monkeys.
t.6.50.15: Those rākṣasas who were the very foremost have been slain in battle by the vānaras, yet I never see any destruction of the vānaras in the fight.
t.6.50.16: So come to my aid, for my treasury is entirely exhausted, and protect this city of Laṅkā, where only children and the aged are left.
t.6.50.17: For your brother's sake, O mighty-armed one, perform this most difficult deed. Never before have I spoken thus to anyone, O brother, scorcher of foes; I have affection for you and the highest regard.
t.6.50.18: O bull among rākṣasas, many times in the clashes between the devas and the asuras, the devas and the asuras were met in battle array and conquered by you in combat. Indeed, among all beings no one is seen who is as mighty as you.
t.6.50.19: Do this supreme thing, dear and beneficial to me, as you please, O lover of battle, O you who are fond of your kinsmen. With your own might scatter the enemy host, as a mighty wind, risen up, scatters an autumn cloud.
